organism_context: Human MTAP (homotrimer, PNP/NP-I fold); archaeal Sulfolobus solfataricus MTAP II; bacterial MtnP. Many bacteria instead use the hydrolytic MTA/SAH nucleosidase (MTN, EC 3.2.2.9), a different protein.
rationale: MTAP is a single-domain purine-nucleoside-phosphorylase-fold trimer with one catalytic activity, phosphorolysis of the N-glycosidic bond of MTA. Some orthologues (Sulfolobus MTAP II, 'MeSAdo/Ado phosphorylase') also accept adenosine, but that is broadened substrate specificity on the same chemistry, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: MTAP functions physiologically only in the phosphorolytic direction (MTA + Pi -> adenine + 5-methylthioribose-1-P) as the committed step of the methionine salvage cycle, which supports the LLM's '>' rather than ModelSEED's MTA-synthesising '<'.

organism_context: Bacterial GuaD (e.g. Klebsiella pneumoniae, E. coli) in the allantoinase/guanine-deaminase gene cluster; mammalian GDA/cypin.
rationale: Guanine deaminase is a single-active-site amidohydrolase-fold (or cytidine-deaminase-fold) Zn enzyme with one catalytic activity, hydrolytic C2 deamination of guanine. Mammalian GDA/cypin additionally binds PSD-95 and promotes tubulin polymerisation, but those are moonlighting (non-catalytic) roles and are excluded by protocol.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination with release of free ammonia is effectively irreversible and the enzyme has no documented aminating activity, so the catabolic direction guanine -> xanthine + NH3 ('>') is the one the enzyme can run; ModelSEED's '<' would require xanthine amination.

enzyme_name: unidentified (EC 1.8.1.3 'hypotaurine dehydrogenase' has never been purified, cloned or assigned a gene)
organism_context: EC 1.8.1.3 derives from an old rat-liver activity. The only molecularly identified hypotaurine -> taurine catalyst is flavin-containing monooxygenase 1 (FMO1), which is NADPH/O2-dependent, not NAD+-dependent.
rationale: No protein has ever been assigned to the NAD+-linked hypotaurine dehydrogenase activity, so the catalysing enzyme cannot be identified and its functionality is genuinely unknown. The nearest characterised enzyme, FMO1, is a monofunctional flavin monooxygenase running a different cofactor chemistry.
direction_note: Every characterised route from hypotaurine to taurine (FMO1, and non-enzymatic oxidation) is an irreversible oxidation, so if any enzyme runs this it is in the taurine-forming direction ('>'); there is no enzymatic precedent for reducing taurine back to hypotaurine with NADH.

enzyme_name: unidentified (EC 2.3.1.10 'hydrogen-sulfide S-acetyltransferase' is a 1961 EC entry resting on a single 1954 report of enzymatic thioltransacetylation; no gene or protein has been assigned)
rationale: The KEGG/IUBMB EC 2.3.1.10 entry carries no organism, gene or sequence and only one 1954 reference (Brady & Stadtman, PMID 13221570), which I did not retrieve through the literature tools; literature searches for a hydrogen-sulfide S-acetyltransferase or a thioacetate-forming acetyl-CoA enzyme returned nothing. The catalysing protein is unknown, so no functionality call is defensible.
direction_note: The one historical assay measured acetyl transfer from acetyl-CoA onto sulfide (thioacetate formation), i.e. left-to-right as written ('>'), but with no identified enzyme neither direction has real enzymological support.

organism_context: Mammalian cytosolic SULTs (human brain/liver arylamine sulfotransferase). Note that bacterial 'arylamine sulfotransferase' (ASST, Eubacterium/Desulfitobacterium) is an unrelated periplasmic enzyme that uses aryl sulfate esters, not PAPS, so it is not the catalyst of this PAPS-dependent reaction.
rationale: The PAPS-dependent N-sulfonation of aniline is carried out by a cytosolic sulfotransferase, a single-domain alpha/beta SULT-fold protein with one PAPS-binding catalytic site and one activity. Enzyme identity is inferred from the cofactor and chemistry plus the purified human brain arylamine sulfotransferase, not from a paper on aniline specifically, hence medium confidence.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation is driven essentially irreversibly by the high group-transfer potential of the PAPS sulfuryl group (PAPS -> PAP), so the sulfonating direction ('>') is the only one cytosolic SULTs run; they cannot regenerate PAPS from PAP.

organism_context: Salmonella typhimurium and E. coli DcyD; Arabidopsis DCD; widespread in Methylobacterium alongside ACC deaminase.
rationale: DcyD is a fold-type II PLP enzyme (ACC-deaminase/tryptophan-synthase-beta family) with a single active site that performs one alpha,beta-elimination on D-cysteine; structural and mutational work on the Salmonella enzyme describes only this activity. It is encoded separately from, not fused to, the related ACC deaminase.
direction_note: The PLP-dependent beta-elimination releases H2S, pyruvate and ammonia irreversibly (the aminoacrylate intermediate hydrolyses spontaneously), so only the degradative direction ('>') is enzymatically accessible; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing H2S, pyruvate and NH3 into D-cysteine.

organism_context: Vertebrate liver/pancreas (rat and human GAMT); conserved back to amphioxus.
rationale: Crystal structures of rat GAMT and its ternary complexes show a single Rossmann-like class-I SAM-methyltransferase domain with one active site and one activity, methyl transfer from SAM to the guanidino nitrogen of guanidinoacetate. No second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and GAMT has no demethylase activity, so the creatine-forming direction ('>') is the only one the enzyme runs; the reverse would require re-methylating SAH, which GAMT cannot do.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; geranyl diphosphate -> iridodial is a lumped multi-enzyme conversion (geraniol synthase -> geraniol 8-hydroxylase CYP76B6 -> 8-hydroxygeraniol oxidoreductase -> iridoid synthase)
organism_context: Catharanthus roseus, Gardenia jasminoides and other iridoid-producing plants; iridoid synthase (ISY) is a member of the progesterone 5beta-reductase family.
rationale: The reaction as written collapses at least four separate catalytic steps run by four unrelated proteins, so there is no single catalysing enzyme to classify; the terminal enzyme, iridoid synthase, is itself a monofunctional NADPH-dependent reductive cyclase. ModelSEED gives this reaction no EC number and no xrefs, consistent with it being a lumped placeholder.
direction_note: The committed step (iridoid synthase, NADPH-dependent reductive cyclisation of 8-oxogeranial) is irreversible toward iridodial, so the biosynthetic direction ('>') is the only plausible one, but the lumped reaction has no single catalyst to anchor a direction call.

organism_context: E. coli and Salmonella enterica thiamine salvage; the eukaryotic salvage enzyme is instead thiamine pyrophosphokinase (EC 2.7.6.2), a different protein.
rationale: ThiK/YcfN was identified as the missing bacterial thiamine kinase and is a small-molecule kinase with a single activity, ATP-dependent phosphorylation of thiamine to thiamine monophosphate. Its secondary contribution to cobinamide salvage is the same phosphotransfer chemistry acting on another substrate, i.e. substrate promiscuity rather than a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: ATP-dependent phosphorylation of a hydroxyl is effectively irreversible under cellular ATP/ADP ratios and a kinase does not run the phosphatase reaction, so the phosphorylating direction ('>') matches the enzymology against ModelSEED's '<'.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana GSDA, a homodimeric cytidine-deaminase-fold Zn enzyme; the plant route generating xanthosine in purine nucleoside catabolism.
rationale: Cocrystal, mutational and dimer-asymmetry studies of AtGSDA describe one zinc active site carrying out a single activity, hydrolytic deamination of guanosine (and 2'-deoxyguanosine, the same chemistry on a related substrate). No second catalytic domain is reported.
direction_note: Hydrolytic deamination releasing free ammonia is irreversible and GSDA is a purely catabolic enzyme feeding xanthosine into purine degradation, so the deaminating direction ('>') is the enzymatically supported one.

enzyme_name: Hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA:quinate hydroxycinnamoyltransferase (HQT; the closely related HCT acts on shikimate)
organism_context: Plant BAHD acyltransferase family: Solanum lycopersicum and S. tuberosum HQT, Lonicera japonica HQT, Cynara (globe artichoke) HQT-like enzymes; chlorogenic/caffeoylquinic acid biosynthesis.
rationale: HQT is a single-chain BAHD acyltransferase with one HXXXD catalytic motif and one activity, transfer of a hydroxycinnamoyl group from CoA to the quinate hydroxyl. Gene-editing and silencing studies treat it as a single-activity enzyme; no second catalytic domain is described.
direction_note: BAHD hydroxycinnamoyl transfer between a CoA thioester and an ester acceptor is genuinely reversible in vitro, so the direction here is set by the acyl-CoA/CoA pool rather than by the enzyme; in planta the ester-forming ('>') direction dominates, which is consistent with the LLM call and makes ModelSEED's hard '<' hard to justify.

enzyme_name: L-pipecolate oxidase / dehydrogenase (sarcosine-oxidase-family FAD amine oxidase; PIPOX)
organism_context: Human peroxisomal L-pipecolic acid oxidase (PIPOX) and the Arabidopsis peroxisomal sarcosine/pipecolate oxidase; both are monomeric-sarcosine-oxidase homologues. Bacterial/mitochondrial L-pipecolate dehydrogenases pass electrons to an acceptor other than O2, as written here.
rationale: PIPOX is a single covalently flavinylated amine-oxidase domain that oxidises both L-pipecolate and sarcosine; that is one catalytic chemistry (flavin-dependent oxidation of a secondary amine) applied to two substrates, which is broad specificity, not bifunctionality. Confidence is medium because the exact protein running the acceptor-linked (EC 1.5.99.3) version of this reaction in a given organism is not pinned down.
direction_note: Flavin-dependent oxidation of pipecolate to the cyclic imine delta-1-piperideine-6-carboxylate is physiologically irreversible (the imine is consumed downstream in lysine degradation), so the oxidative direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; the C18->C20 acyl-CoA elongation is run by the four-component fatty acid elongase system (condensing enzyme KCS/ELOVL, 3-oxoacyl-CoA reductase, 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratase, enoyl-CoA reductase). The acyltransferase step named here is the condensing enzyme.
organism_context: Plant (FAE1/KCS) and animal (ELOVL) endoplasmic-reticulum elongase systems; also a membrane elongase complex in fungi such as Magnaporthe oryzae.
rationale: EC 2.3.1.119 (icosanoyl-CoA synthase) was deleted by IUBMB in 2015 precisely because it is not one enzyme: it is now covered by EC 2.3.1.199, 1.1.1.330, 4.2.1.134 and 1.3.1.93, four separate monofunctional polypeptides that associate as a membrane elongase complex. Per protocol this is a multi-subunit system, not a fused bifunctional enzyme, so the condensing subunit that carries the named acyltransferase step is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: Condensation is driven irreversibly by decarboxylation of malonyl-CoA and the cycle is completed by two irreversible NAD(P)H reductions, so elongation runs only toward icosanoyl-CoA ('>'); note also that elongases use NADPH, so this NADH-linked variant is the non-physiological twin of rxn01592.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; the C18->C20 acyl-CoA elongation is run by the four-component fatty acid elongase system (condensing enzyme KCS/ELOVL, 3-oxoacyl-CoA reductase, 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratase, enoyl-CoA reductase). The acyltransferase step named here is the condensing enzyme.
organism_context: Plant (FAE1/KCS) and animal (ELOVL) endoplasmic-reticulum elongase systems; also a membrane elongase complex in fungi such as Magnaporthe oryzae.
rationale: Same system as rxn01591 but with the physiological NADPH cofactor. EC 2.3.1.119 was deleted and split into EC 2.3.1.199, 1.1.1.330, 4.2.1.134 and 1.3.1.93, i.e. four separate monofunctional proteins forming a membrane complex, which the protocol treats as a complex rather than a fused bi/polyfunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylative condensation plus two NADPH-dependent reductions make the elongation cycle irreversible toward icosanoyl-CoA ('>'); there is no enzyme that reverses it (beta-oxidation is a separate pathway with different chemistry), so ModelSEED's '<' is not enzymatically supported.

organism_context: Trypanosoma cruzi formiminoglutamase (structurally characterised); bacterial HutG in the Bacillus/Pseudomonas histidine utilisation (hut) operons.
rationale: Formiminoglutamase is an arginase-like binuclear manganese metalloenzyme of the ureohydrolase superfamily with a single active site and one activity, hydrolysis of the formimidoyl amide of N-formimino-L-glutamate. It is a standalone protein in the hut operon, not fused to the other histidine-degradation enzymes.
direction_note: Amide hydrolysis releasing formamide is irreversible and HutG is a purely catabolic step of histidine degradation, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the enzymatic one; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing glutamate with formamide.

organism_context: Fused as one polypeptide in vertebrates (pig and human liver FTCD, a circular Golgi-associated homo-octamer). In Clostridium cylindrosporum the two activities sit on separate proteins, so the fusion is lineage-specific.
rationale: FTCD is a single ~58 kDa chain carrying two genuinely distinct catalytic activities on two separable domains: an N-terminal glutamate formimidoyltransferase (EC 2.1.2.5) and a C-terminal formimidoyltetrahydrofolate cyclodeaminase (EC 4.3.1.4); the isolated domains fold and dimerise independently, and the crystal structure of the bifunctional octamer shows both active sites. This reaction is run by the cyclodeaminase domain.
direction_note: This is exactly the bifunctional-architecture case the protocol flags: the two domains are arranged around a circular octamer so that 5-formimino-THF made by the transferase domain is channelled directly into the cyclodeaminase domain, which drives flux unidirectionally to 5,10-methenyl-THF + NH3 ('>'); the reverse (ammonia addition across methenyl-THF) does not occur in vivo, so ModelSEED's '<' conflicts with the channelling architecture.

enzyme_name: unidentified (KEGG flags R08699 as an incomplete reaction with an unidentified donor; no EC number and no KO are assigned)
organism_context: The characterised biological route to L-cysteate is cysteate synthase acting on O-phospho-L-serine plus sulfite in methanogens, not a PAPS-dependent C-sulfotransferase.
rationale: KEGG itself annotates R08699 as an incomplete reaction with an unidentified donor and assigns it neither an EC number nor an orthology group, and literature searching turned up no PAPS:2-aminoacrylate C-sulfotransferase. No catalysing protein exists to classify.
direction_note: With the donor step explicitly unidentified in KEGG, neither direction has enzymological support; the real cysteate-forming chemistry uses a different donor (sulfite) and a different enzyme, so this reaction should probably not be carrying a direction constraint at all.

organism_context: Classically a secreted fungal activity (Aspergillus flavus); the modern molecular equivalents are GH78/GH106 alpha-L-rhamnosidases from fungi (Alternaria), bacteria (Novosphingobium RHA-P) and gut Bifidobacterium/Bacteroides.
rationale: No gene has ever been cloned under the name 'quercitrinase'; the activity is carried by alpha-L-rhamnosidases, which are single-catalytic-domain glycoside hydrolases with one activity (several carry additional non-catalytic carbohydrate-binding or beta-sandwich domains, which do not count). Confidence is low because the enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry and from rhamnosidase literature rather than from a paper on this exact reaction.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis in bulk water is effectively irreversible, so the aglycone-releasing direction ('>') is the only one a hydrolase runs; ModelSEED's '<' would require a transglycosylation/synthase reaction these enzymes do not perform at physiological rhamnose concentrations.

distinct_activities: acyl-CoA dehydrogenation of glutaryl-CoA to glutaconyl-CoA (EC 1.3.8.6)
decarboxylation of the glutaconyl-CoA intermediate to crotonyl-CoA + CO2
organism_context: Human mitochondrial GCDH (homotetramer of one polypeptide); bacterial decarboxylating GCDHs. Non-decarboxylating glutaryl-CoA dehydrogenases, which perform only the dehydrogenation, exist in anaerobic aromatic degraders such as Desulfococcus multivorans.
rationale: One polypeptide performs two chemically distinct catalytic steps, FAD-dependent alpha,beta-dehydrogenation and then decarboxylation of the glutaconyl-CoA intermediate; the crystal structures are explicitly described as giving the 'structural bases of dehydrogenation and decarboxylation reactions', and a decarboxylating GCDH can be converted into a non-decarboxylating one by site-directed mutagenesis, showing the two activities are separable. Caveat behind the medium confidence: both steps occur in a single active site within one catalytic cycle rather than on two fused domains, so a stricter reading would score this monofunctional.
direction_note: The decarboxylation half of the bifunctionality is what makes the overall reaction irreversible: loss of CO2 pulls it to crotonyl-CoA ('>'), and no enzyme carboxylates crotonyl-CoA back to glutaryl-CoA, so ModelSEED's '<' is not enzymatically achievable.

enzyme_name: Amidase (amidase-signature family wide-spectrum amidase hydrolysing 2-phenylacetamide; e.g. Pseudomonas aeruginosa AmiE-type and Rhodococcus amidases)
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa amidase (the acetanilide/phenylacetamide-utilising system) and Rhodococcus erythropolis amidases; amidase-signature (AS) superfamily, which is also widespread in plants.
rationale: These are single-domain Ser-cisSer-Lys amidase-signature hydrolases with one catalytic activity, hydrolysis of the amide C-N bond. The acyl-transfer side reaction (transfer to hydroxylamine giving hydroxamates) proceeds through the same acyl-enzyme intermediate with a different acceptor nucleophile and is therefore not a second catalytic activity. Medium confidence because ModelSEED names only a generic 'probable amidase' rather than one characterised protein.
direction_note: Amide hydrolysis to the carboxylate plus ammonia is irreversible in water, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the one the enzyme runs; the reverse amide synthesis requires non-physiological ammonia levels and proceeds by acyl transfer, not by reversal.

enzyme_name: unidentified cytidylyltransferase for 2-trimethylaminoethylphosphonate (ModelSEED assigns EC 2.7.7.15, choline-phosphate cytidylyltransferase, but the substrate here is a C-P phosphonate, not choline phosphate)
organism_context: Phosphonolipid-producing bacteria and protists; bacterial phosphonate pathways are known to use dedicated CTP/other nucleotidyltransferases to activate phosphonates.
rationale: No protein has been shown to make CMP-2-trimethylaminoethylphosphonate; the EC 2.7.7.15 assignment is a chemistry-based transfer from choline-phosphate cytidylyltransferase, whose real substrate this is not. The nominal EC 2.7.7.15 enzyme (CCT/Pcyt1) is itself a monofunctional nucleotidyltransferase whose extra amphipathic-helix membrane-binding segment is regulatory, not catalytic, but that does not establish the catalyst of this reaction.
direction_note: All CTP-dependent cytidylyltransferases are pulled forward in vivo by pyrophosphatase hydrolysis of the released PPi, so the CMP-adduct-forming direction ('>') is the physiological one even though the isolated nucleotidyl transfer is near-equilibrium.

organism_context: Pinus contorta (lodgepole pine) xylem CBG, cloned and heterologously expressed; Arabidopsis BGLU45/BGLU46 hydrolyse monolignol glucosides; also characterised in Picea and Pinus sylvestris xylem.
rationale: Coniferin beta-glucosidase is a family GH1 retaining beta-glucosidase, a single (beta/alpha)8-barrel catalytic domain with one activity, hydrolysis of the beta-glucosidic bond of coniferin to release coniferyl alcohol. No second catalytic activity is described.
direction_note: GH1 glucoside hydrolysis is irreversible under cellular water activity and the physiological role is to release coniferyl alcohol for lignification, so the hydrolytic direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

organism_context: Flaveria chloraefolia and Flaveria bidentis; one of a set of position-specific plant cytosolic flavonol sulfotransferases (3-ST, 3'-ST, 4'-ST) that act sequentially.
rationale: The Flaveria flavonol sulfotransferases were purified and cloned as separate, strictly position-specific single-domain cytosolic PAPS-dependent sulfotransferases; the 3'-ST carries one catalytic activity and acts only on quercetin 3-sulfate. Medium confidence because the published purification and mutagenesis work focuses on the 3-sulfotransferase, with the 3'-enzyme characterised as a distinct member of the same monofunctional family.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation runs irreversibly in the sulfo-transfer direction (PAPS consumed to PAP) and these plant STs act in an obligate 3- then 3'- sequence, so the bissulfate-forming direction ('>') is the enzymatic one.

organism_context: Human mitochondrial ACAD8 (homotetramer), the valine-degradation acyl-CoA dehydrogenase; plant/Arabidopsis homologue in branched-chain amino acid catabolism.
rationale: ACAD8 is a classical homotetrameric FAD acyl-CoA dehydrogenase: one subunit type, one active site, one activity (alpha,beta-dehydrogenation of isobutyryl-CoA to methacrylyl-CoA). Its documented substrate promiscuity across short branched-chain acyl-CoAs is specificity breadth, not a second catalytic activity, and unlike GCDH it does not decarboxylate.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases hand electrons to ETF rather than to free FAD, and ETF/ETF-QO coupling pulls the reaction irreversibly toward the enoyl-CoA ('>'); the near-zero free energy that the free-FAD/FADH2 couple in this written equation implies is an artefact of the cofactor representation, which plausibly explains why ModelSEED lands on '<'.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; KEGG annotates R02721 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC and no KO. The real route to the thiamine thiazole goes via DXP synthase (pyruvate + G3P -> 1-deoxy-D-xylulose 5-phosphate) and then thiazole synthase ThiG with ThiH/ThiO and ThiS-thiocarboxylate (bacteria) or THI4 (yeast/plants).
organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli/Bacillus ThiGHS or ThiGOS) and fungi/plants (suicide enzyme THI4).
rationale: KEGG explicitly flags R02721 as unclear and gives it no enzyme, orthology or pathway link, and the reaction as written lumps at least two committed steps carried out by unrelated proteins, so there is no catalysing enzyme to classify.
direction_note: The real thiazole-forming steps (ThiGH, or the suicide enzyme THI4, which is consumed in a single turnover) are strictly irreversible biosynthetic reactions, consistent with '>' as written, but no single catalyst exists to justify a direction constraint on this lumped reaction.
